items.name: Hands-free Theatre Door
items.summary: A hermetically sealed sliding door opened by a foot sensor, so hands stay clean and the room keeps its positive air pressure.
points: Activate it with your foot - never push the door or handle with your hands.
Keep doors closed: every opening disturbs the clean airflow and raises infection risk.
The light above shows IN USE or VACANT.
Main door is for patient entry and exit on the trolley.
items.nurseRole: Limit traffic through the door and never prop it open during surgery.

items.name: Laminar Airflow Canopy
items.summary: An ultra-clean ventilation ceiling that pushes HEPA-filtered air straight down over the operating table.
points: Creates a clean zone over the sterile field and the instrument trolleys.
Theatre air is kept at positive pressure so air flows out of the room, not in.
Typical theatre conditions: temperature 18 to 23 degrees Celsius, humidity 40 to 60 percent.
Do not place tall equipment or lean over the field in a way that blocks the downward airflow.
items.nurseRole: Keep trolleys and the sterile field inside the clean-air zone.

items.name: Surgical Lights (Main and Satellite)
items.summary: Two shadow-free LED operating lights on articulated ceiling arms, focused on the surgical site.
points: The larger main light and smaller satellite light overlap to remove shadows.
The centre handle is covered with a sterile handle cover - only scrubbed staff may touch it.
Non-sterile staff adjust lights only using the outer handle, and only when asked.
LED lights produce very little heat, protecting exposed tissues.
items.nurseRole: Position lights before draping and never touch the sterile handle when you are not scrubbed.

items.name: Anaesthesia Ceiling Pendant
items.summary: A ceiling-mounted supply column beside the anaesthetic machine that delivers medical gases, suction, power and data.
points: Gas outlets are colour coded: oxygen white, nitrous oxide blue, medical air black, vacuum yellow.
Each outlet only accepts its own gas-specific probe, preventing wrong connections.
Keeps cables and hoses off the floor, reducing trip hazards.
items.nurseRole: Check the gas outlets and suction before the list starts.

items.name: Surgical Ceiling Pendant
items.summary: A second supply column on the surgical side that powers the diathermy, suction and other surgical equipment.
points: Holds equipment on shelves above the floor.
Provides vacuum outlets for surgical suction.
Reduces cables on the floor.
items.nurseRole: Connect equipment to the pendant rather than to floor extension leads.

items.name: Operating Table
items.summary: An electro-hydraulic table with movable head, back, seat and leg sections, so the patient can be safely positioned for each operation.
points: Height and tilt are adjusted using the hand control.
Arm boards must never be extended beyond 90 degrees, to prevent brachial plexus injury.
A safety strap is placed across the thighs before anaesthesia.
Gel pads protect pressure areas: head, elbows, sacrum and heels.
Lock the table and brakes before transferring the patient.
items.nurseRole: Help position the patient safely, protect pressure areas and keep the patient's dignity and warmth.

items.name: Anaesthetic Screen
items.summary: A stainless bar at the head of the table that holds the drapes up, separating the sterile field from the anaesthetist's area.
points: Marks the boundary between the sterile and non-sterile areas.
Lets the anaesthetist reach the patient's airway without contaminating the field.
items.nurseRole: Make sure the drape is secured to the screen and does not cover the airway.

items.name: Mayo Instrument Stand
items.summary: A height-adjustable tray placed over the patient's legs that holds the instruments needed right now.
points: Draped with a sterile cover and set up by the scrub nurse.
Holds only the instruments in immediate use - the rest stay on the back trolley.
Its base slides under the operating table.
items.nurseRole: Only the scrubbed team touches the top of the Mayo stand.

items.name: Instrument Trolley (Back Table)
items.summary: A large stainless steel trolley covered with a sterile drape where the full instrument set, bowls and swabs are laid out.
points: Prepared using an aseptic technique: clean the trolley, open the outer pack, then the scrubbed nurse lays it out.
Only the top of a draped trolley is sterile - the sides below table height are not.
Never reach across a sterile trolley; keep 30 centimetres away if you are not scrubbed.
Instruments are counted before, during and at the end of surgery.
items.nurseRole: Prepare and protect the sterile trolley and help with the counts.

items.name: Diathermy (Electrosurgical Unit)
items.summary: A generator that uses high-frequency electricity to cut tissue and seal bleeding vessels.
points: Monopolar diathermy needs a patient return electrode (plate) on clean, dry, hair-free skin over a large muscle.
Yellow means CUT and blue means COAG on the pencil and the foot pedal.
Keep the pencil in its holster when not in use, to prevent burns and fires.
Remove metal jewellery and keep alcohol-based skin preps dry before use.
items.nurseRole: Apply the return electrode correctly and check the skin under it after surgery.

items.name: Surgical Suction Unit
items.summary: A vacuum regulator with collection canisters that removes blood and fluids from the surgical site.
points: Connects to the yellow vacuum outlet on the pendant.
The Yankauer sucker is used for the field or for the patient's airway.
Always have working suction ready before anaesthesia starts.
Canister contents help estimate blood loss.
items.nurseRole: Check suction before every case and record fluid in the canisters.

items.name: Kick Bucket (Swab Bucket)
items.summary: A low stainless bucket on wheels where used swabs are dropped so they can be counted.
points: Used swabs are later separated and displayed for the swab count.
Moved with the foot, keeping hands clean.
items.nurseRole: Use it for counts: never remove swabs from the theatre until the final count is correct.

items.name: Swab and Instrument Count Board
items.summary: A whiteboard where the scrub and circulating nurses record swabs, needles, blades and instruments.
points: Counts are done before the operation, before closing a cavity, and at skin closure.
Two nurses count aloud together.
Any discrepancy must be reported to the surgeon immediately.
items.nurseRole: Record counts accurately to prevent retained surgical items.

items.name: Anaesthesia Machine
items.summary: A workstation that delivers oxygen, air and anaesthetic vapour, and ventilates the patient.
points: Flowmeters control oxygen, air and nitrous oxide.
Vaporisers add volatile agents such as sevoflurane (yellow) and isoflurane (purple).
The emergency oxygen flush button gives a high flow of pure oxygen.
The breathing circuit and reservoir bag connect to the patient's face mask or airway.
It is checked by the anaesthetist before every list.
items.nurseRole: Assist the anaesthetist, keep the area tidy and never adjust settings yourself.

items.name: Patient Monitor
items.summary: A multi-parameter monitor that displays the patient's vital signs continuously during surgery.
points: ECG and heart rate, oxygen saturation (SpO2), blood pressure, end-tidal carbon dioxide and temperature.
Alarms sound when a value goes outside safe limits - always respond.
Normal adult SpO2 is 95 to 100 percent.
items.nurseRole: Observe the patient's condition continuously and report changes promptly.

items.name: Anaesthetic Trolley
items.summary: A drawer cart that holds airway equipment, IV access items, drugs and fluids for the anaesthetist.
points: Drawers are organised and labelled: airway, IV access, drugs, fluids, emergency.
Drugs are drawn up and labelled immediately with the drug name, dose and time.
Controlled drugs are stored locked and checked by two people.
items.nurseRole: Help keep it stocked and follow the rights of medication administration.

items.name: Sharps Container
items.summary: A yellow rigid container for needles, blades and other sharps.
points: Dispose of sharps immediately at the point of use.
Never re-sheath needles.
Close and replace it when it reaches the fill line (three-quarters full).
Report any needle-stick injury immediately.
items.nurseRole: Safe sharps disposal protects you and your colleagues.

items.name: IV Drip Stand
items.summary: A wheeled stand that holds intravenous fluid bags and giving sets above the patient.
points: The bag hangs higher than the patient so fluid flows by gravity.
The drip chamber is half filled; the roller clamp controls the rate.
Check the fluid, its expiry date and the cannula site before connecting.
items.nurseRole: Prime giving sets without air and check the rights before administering IV fluids.

items.name: IV Stand with Pumps
items.summary: A second drip stand carrying the infusion pump and syringe driver.
points: Used when fluids or drugs must run at an exact rate.
items.nurseRole: Double-check pump settings against the prescription.

items.name: Infusion Pump and Syringe Driver
items.summary: Electronic pumps that give IV fluids and drugs at a precise, programmed rate.
points: The volumetric pump is used for fluids; the syringe driver for small, accurate drug doses.
Rate, volume and drug name are programmed and checked against the prescription.
Occlusion and air-in-line alarms must be acted on immediately.
items.nurseRole: Follow the rights of medication administration and monitor the infusion site.

items.name: Forced-air Patient Warmer
items.summary: A warming unit that blows warm air into a disposable blanket over the patient.
points: Prevents inadvertent peri-operative hypothermia.
The aim is to keep core temperature at or above 36 degrees Celsius.
Never place the hose directly on the skin without the blanket.
items.nurseRole: Monitor the patient's temperature and keep them covered.

items.name: Fluid Warming Cabinet
items.summary: A cabinet that keeps IV and irrigation fluids warm, around 37 degrees Celsius.
points: Warm fluids help prevent hypothermia.
Check the temperature display and expiry dates.
items.nurseRole: Use warmed fluids when they are prescribed or requested.

items.name: Emergency Trolley and Defibrillator
items.summary: A red trolley with resuscitation drugs, airway equipment and a defibrillator for cardiac arrest.
points: It is sealed with a tag and checked every day.
Know where it is before every case - seconds matter.
The defibrillator delivers a shock for shockable rhythms; stand clear when told.
items.nurseRole: Bring the emergency trolley immediately and follow the resuscitation team leader.

items.name: Clinical Waste Bin (Yellow)
items.summary: A foot-pedal bin for infectious waste contaminated with blood or body fluids.
points: Yellow is used for infectious clinical waste.
The pedal lid keeps your hands clean.
Follow your hospital's colour-coding policy.
items.nurseRole: Segregate waste correctly at the point of use.

items.name: General Waste Bin (Black)
items.summary: A foot-pedal bin for non-infectious general waste such as packaging paper.
points: Black is for general, non-contaminated waste.
Never put sharps or contaminated items here.
items.nurseRole: Keep general and clinical waste separate.

items.name: Linen Skip
items.summary: A pedal-operated hamper for used linen and gowns.
points: Used linen is handled carefully and not shaken.
Soiled linen goes in the correct bag.
items.nurseRole: Dispose of used gowns and linen correctly after the case.

items.name: Documentation Workstation
items.summary: Two computers: one for nursing records and one for the surgical team's notes and results.
points: The nursing computer records the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist, counts and care.
The second computer shows operation notes and blood results.
Sign In, Time Out and Sign Out are the three checklist stages.
items.nurseRole: Document care accurately and complete the safety checklist.

items.name: Imaging (PACS) Monitor
items.summary: A large wall screen that displays the patient's X-rays and CT scans during surgery.
points: Confirms the correct side and site.
Images are checked during Time Out.
items.nurseRole: Make sure the correct patient's images are displayed.

items.name: Teaching Monitor
items.summary: A screen that shows the operation from a camera so students can observe safely.
points: Lets you watch without crowding the sterile field.
items.nurseRole: Observe from a safe distance and ask questions at an appropriate time.

items.name: Theatre Control Panel
items.summary: A wall panel with the clock, operation timers, and controls for temperature, humidity, airflow and lights.
points: Theatre temperature is usually 18 to 23 degrees Celsius.
Humidity is kept between 40 and 60 percent.
The timer records anaesthesia and surgery times.
items.nurseRole: Record times accurately and report any ventilation alarm.

items.name: Wall Gas Outlets and Alarm Panel
items.summary: Back-up medical gas outlets and an alarm panel showing pipeline pressures.
points: Colour codes: oxygen white, nitrous oxide blue, medical air black, vacuum yellow.
An alarm means the gas supply pressure is abnormal - report it immediately.
items.nurseRole: Know the colour codes so the right gas reaches the patient.

items.name: Sterile Supply Cabinet
items.summary: Glass-fronted cabinets that store wrapped sterile instrument sets, gowns, gloves and drapes.
points: Before opening a pack, check the indicator tape has changed colour.
Check the expiry date and that the wrapping is dry and intact.
Use first-in, first-out stock rotation.
Store packs off the floor, in a clean and dry place.
items.nurseRole: Check every sterile pack before you open it - if in doubt, do not use it.

items.name: Positioning Aids
items.summary: Gel head rings, chest rolls, heel pads, arm supports and straps used to position the patient.
points: Protect bony prominences to prevent pressure injury.
Support joints in a neutral position.
Choose aids for supine, lateral, prone or lithotomy positions.
items.nurseRole: Position the patient with the team and check pressure areas.

items.name: Lead Aprons (Radiation PPE)
items.summary: Lead aprons and thyroid collars worn when X-ray imaging is used during surgery.
points: Time, distance and shielding reduce radiation exposure.
Hang aprons flat - folding them cracks the lead.
items.nurseRole: Wear a lead apron and thyroid collar whenever an image intensifier is in use.

items.name: Specimen Station
items.summary: Specimen pots, request forms and biohazard bags for tissue taken during surgery.
points: Label every specimen with the patient's details, specimen type and date.
Check the specimen and form with the surgeon before sending it.
items.nurseRole: Correctly label and dispatch every specimen.

items.name: Fire Extinguisher and Alarm
items.summary: A CO2 fire extinguisher and manual fire-alarm call point.
points: CO2 extinguishers are safe on electrical equipment.
The fire triangle in theatre: oxygen, heat (diathermy) and fuel (drapes, alcohol preps).
Follow the person in charge during an alarm.
items.nurseRole: Know the fire plan and the location of the extinguisher.

items.name: Intercom Telephone
items.summary: A wall phone to contact the theatre reception, laboratory or emergency team.
points: Use it to call for help without leaving the patient.
items.nurseRole: Know the emergency numbers.

items.name: Alcohol Hand Rub Dispenser
items.summary: An elbow-operated dispenser of alcohol hand rub for hand hygiene.
points: Use it before and after patient contact (WHO five moments).
It does not replace the surgical scrub for the sterile team.
items.nurseRole: Clean your hands every time you enter or leave the patient area.

items.name: Alcohol Hand Rub (Corridor)
items.summary: Hand rub at the theatre entrance.
points: Clean your hands before entering the theatre.
items.nurseRole: Perform hand hygiene before entering.

items.name: Surgical Scrub Sink
items.summary: A deep sink with sensor-operated taps where the sterile team performs the surgical hand scrub.
points: Remove jewellery, keep nails short and wear a cap and mask before scrubbing.
Scrub hands and forearms for 3 to 5 minutes with chlorhexidine or povidone-iodine.
Keep hands above the elbows so water runs away from the hands.
Dry with a sterile towel, then put on a sterile gown and gloves (closed gloving).
items.nurseRole: Perform a correct surgical scrub before gowning and gloving.

items.name: PPE and Theatre Attire Trolley
items.summary: A trolley with caps, masks, eye protection, sterile gowns and sterile gloves in different sizes.
points: Theatre attire: scrub suit, cap covering all hair, mask covering nose and mouth.
Eye protection guards against splashes.
Sterile gown and gloves are put on after the surgical scrub.
Gloves come in sizes from 6 to 8.5.
items.nurseRole: Wear correct attire and help the team gown and glove.

items.name: Theatre Footwear
items.summary: Dedicated theatre clogs worn only inside the theatre suite.
points: Closed, washable shoes protect your feet from sharps and spills.
items.nurseRole: Change into theatre footwear before entering.

items.name: Step-up Stool
items.summary: A stainless step that raises a team member to the right working height.
points: Used by surgeons or scrub nurses of different heights.
items.nurseRole: Place it where needed without breaking sterility.

items.name: Theatre Stool
items.summary: A height-adjustable stool for seated procedures or the anaesthetist.
points: Its height adjusts by gas lift.

items.name: Door to the Anaesthetic Room
items.summary: Leads to the anaesthetic room where the patient may be anaesthetised before entering theatre.
points: Keeps the patient calm, away from the view of the theatre.

items.name: Door to the Dirty Utility
items.summary: Leads to the dirty utility room for waste, used instruments and soiled linen.
points: Dirty items leave by this route so they do not cross clean areas.

items.name: Door to the Preparation (Lay-up) Room
items.summary: Leads to the room where sterile trolleys and supplies are prepared.
points: Clean and sterile items enter through here.

items.name: Door to the Scrub Room
items.summary: Leads to the scrub room used by the surgical team.
points: The team enters theatre gowned and gloved.

items.name: Scalpel (No. 3 handle, No. 10 blade)
items.summary: Used to make the skin incision. Blades are attached and removed with a needle holder, never with fingers.
points: Used to make the skin incision. Blades are attached and removed with a needle holder, never with fingers.
items.nurseRole: Hand instruments to the surgeon correctly and count them.

items.name: Mayo Scissors (curved)
items.summary: Heavy scissors for cutting tough tissue and sutures.
points: Heavy scissors for cutting tough tissue and sutures.
items.nurseRole: Hand instruments to the surgeon correctly and count them.

items.name: Metzenbaum Scissors
items.summary: Long, fine scissors for delicate tissue dissection.
points: Long, fine scissors for delicate tissue dissection.
items.nurseRole: Hand instruments to the surgeon correctly and count them.

items.name: Artery Forceps (curved)
items.summary: Clamps bleeding vessels before they are tied or sealed.
points: Clamps bleeding vessels before they are tied or sealed.
items.nurseRole: Hand instruments to the surgeon correctly and count them.

items.name: Mosquito Artery Forceps
items.summary: Small fine clamps for small vessels.
points: Small fine clamps for small vessels.
items.nurseRole: Hand instruments to the surgeon correctly and count them.

items.name: Needle Holder (Mayo-Hegar)
items.summary: Holds the suture needle; gold rings show tungsten carbide jaws.
points: Holds the suture needle; gold rings show tungsten carbide jaws.
items.nurseRole: Hand instruments to the surgeon correctly and count them.

items.name: Allis Tissue Forceps
items.summary: Grasps and holds tissue firmly.
points: Grasps and holds tissue firmly.
items.nurseRole: Hand instruments to the surgeon correctly and count them.

items.name: Sponge Holding Forceps
items.summary: Holds swabs for skin preparation or deep swabbing.
points: Holds swabs for skin preparation or deep swabbing.
items.nurseRole: Hand instruments to the surgeon correctly and count them.

items.name: Towel Clip
items.summary: Secures drapes in place.
points: Secures drapes in place.
items.nurseRole: Hand instruments to the surgeon correctly and count them.

items.name: Toothed Dissecting Forceps
items.summary: Holds tough tissue such as skin.
points: Holds tough tissue such as skin.
items.nurseRole: Hand instruments to the surgeon correctly and count them.

items.name: Non-toothed Dissecting Forceps
items.summary: Holds delicate tissue and vessels.
points: Holds delicate tissue and vessels.
items.nurseRole: Hand instruments to the surgeon correctly and count them.

items.name: Langenbeck Retractor
items.summary: Holds the wound edges open.
points: Holds the wound edges open.
items.nurseRole: Hand instruments to the surgeon correctly and count them.

items.name: Kidney Dish
items.summary: Receives used instruments, swabs or small items.
points: Receives used instruments, swabs or small items.
items.nurseRole: Hand instruments to the surgeon correctly and count them.

items.name: Gallipot
items.summary: A small bowl for skin preparation solution or saline.
points: A small bowl for skin preparation solution or saline.
items.nurseRole: Hand instruments to the surgeon correctly and count them.

items.name: Gauze Swabs (X-ray detectable)
items.summary: Absorb blood; the blue thread shows on X-ray. Every swab is counted.
points: Absorb blood; the blue thread shows on X-ray. Every swab is counted.
items.nurseRole: Hand instruments to the surgeon correctly and count them.

items.name: Suture Pack
items.summary: Contains the suture material and needle; opened onto the sterile field when needed.
points: Contains the suture material and needle; opened onto the sterile field when needed.
items.nurseRole: Hand instruments to the surgeon correctly and count them.

items.summary: The operating room itself.
